chapter_theme: Salutary teaching (இதோபதேசம்): leave the passing birth behind, hold the Lord in mind even at death, keep to the Siva way with truth and love, and worship the guru who shows how to reach him; for those who do, deeds and births end.
structure_note: Direct exhortations in the second person (2102 to 2113), then verses on whom the Lord rewards and whom he punishes (2114 to 2118), and a close on the guru as the way to the Lord (2119, 2120).

2102.reading: Forget and leave the birth that does not last on this earth; even at the time of dying, think of the Lord; contemplate the excellent Siva way that ends the suffering of fluttering in distress.
2102.nuance: இறந்தொழி காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும் returns almost word for word in 2108: the thought held at death matters for what follows.

2103.reading: Direct your mind as far as it will go; speak the truth as well as you can; even if you have nothing, our Lord is there in fullness; seek the good way of Hara.
2103.nuance: இல்லை எனினும் can be 'even if you lack means' or 'even if some say he is not'; both readings make the Lord's presence independent of the seeker's state.

2104.reading: Kin is one and God is one; think only good; then there is no death for you and no shame; there is no refuge to go to outside your own mind; stand there, think of him firmly and be saved.
2104.nuance: ஒன்றே குலம் is now usually read as the one kinship of all people; it may also mean all souls are of one kind. நமன் இல்லை நாணாமே can be 'there is no Yama, without shame', or 'there is no Yama, be unashamed'; line 3 may be 'there is no state you will enter' rather than 'no refuge outside the mind'.

2105.reading: Praise the lord of the cool Kailasa mountain, the Nambi who is the centre of the four directions, and, taking up the body that wafts its fragrance to the winds, stand telling the nature of the one who kicked Death, and be saved.
2105.nuance: கூற்று உதைத்தான் is Siva who kicked Yama to save Markandeya. Line 3 (காற்றிசைக்கும் கமழ் ஆக்கை) is obscure: perhaps the body made fragrant by worship, or the body of breath.

2106.reading: Seek the way to go so that, leaving this body, you do not enter another body and be born; if you think on that time, asking when this body came to be ours, grace may be gained.
2106.nuance: அக்காலம் உன்ன may be reflecting on the body's origin, or holding the Lord in mind at the time of leaving it, as in 2102 and 2108.

2107.reading: Hara is there as knower of that thing that enters as it leaves, even as it comes to be; even when dying, seek the Lord, and that thing which comes to be will reach the farther shore.
2107.nuance: அப்பொருள் (that thing) is read as the soul, which passes from body to body; அக்கரை (the other shore) is release from that passing.

2108.reading: If the one that flies is to reach its goal, think of the Lord even at the time of dying; then the state of Siva joins with distinction, and after it comes freedom from all birth, the great world.
2108.nuance: பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று (the thing that flies) is the soul, as a bird leaving its nest.

2109.reading: Gathering and standing, worship our Lord; singing, stand within and bow at his feet; for those who stand within the mirror and come to know, he becomes like a cow long in milk after calving.
2109.nuance: ஆடி (mirror) may also be read as 'dancing'. பசு is both cow and the soul; the image of the milch cow is usually taken as the Lord giving freely, but whether the soul or the Lord is the cow is not fixed.

2110.reading: When the releasing one rises upward, stand in the middle and seek the Lord's feet; the one of unfailing fame, by whom strong deeds perish, will place you among the celestials.
2110.nuance: விடுகின்ற சிவனார் may be a slip for சீவனார், the soul leaving the body; நடுநின்று may be the middle channel of yoga or the space between the brows. Read either as death or as yogic ascent.

2111.reading: Those who wear the holy ash, crying 'you who ride the bull, our Lord, our master', are devotees and living gods; those who wear as their ornament the holy feet of the great one with the river in his red locks have no deeds left to bind them.
2111.nuance: வேறு அணிவார் may mean they wear the feet as a distinct ornament, or wear nothing else.

2112.reading: You who would have joy, know our Lord and be loving, take on the quality of the true knowledge that austerity yields; standing in the work of birth, you have toiled in the bond that brings pain and been ruined.
2112.nuance: The verse moves from what one may become to what one has been: the same addressees, offered love and knowledge, are told they have so far only laboured in பாசம்.

2113.reading: There is one true austerity to take up, one true foot to take hold of, one true path to take up, for those who stand wishing to take them up.
2113.nuance: மெய்த்தாள் is read as the Lord's true feet. The last line puts the condition on the seeker's wanting: the way exists for whoever desires it.

2114.reading: The fire-coloured one gives joy to those who come to him and painful birth to those who turn away; to the keen he shows his ringing anklets there, and those who join him come to know the God.
2114.nuance: The verse states a simple reciprocity: drawing near gives joy, turning away gives birth again.

2115.reading: They praise for all time release, knowledge, the sound of threefold Tamil and the Lord; the Stainless one is there as ghee within milk, yet they do not desire that light.
2115.nuance: The ghee in milk is the Lord present throughout but not seen until churned out. The last line may fault those who praise but do not seek the light, or (taking விரும்பார் as 'want nothing else') praise them; the reading here takes the first.

2116.reading: No one can tell how many ages the Stainless one, lord of order, has set; except that they come and plunge into birth, they cannot understand anything of Siva.
2116.nuance: நியமத்தன் may be the lord of cosmic order or the one who keeps the observances. பவமத்து and சிவமத்து are unusual forms.

2117.reading: Whatever the life here and whatever its ills, at the time like sleep, none but those free of venom can seek you, pure gem-coloured one, the Vikirta dwelling in excellence.
2117.nuance: துஞ்சு ஒத்த காலம் is read as death, likened to sleep. நஞ்சு அற்றவர் (those without poison) may be those free of malice or of the soul's impurity. The verse is obscure and the reading tentative.

2118.reading: If deceivers stay in the land before the true guru, famine comes to it; the Lord fears them and casts them into hard hell, while for those with upright hearts, attainment is there to be seen.
2118.nuance: The text is doubtful throughout: சற்குறுபால் is probably சற்குரு, அஞ்சுவன் (he fears) is odd for the Lord, and தெரிசிக்க சித்தியே may mean seeing them is itself an attainment. Only the broad contrast of deceivers and the upright is secure.

2119.reading: Countless gods worshipped Siva, yet by worshipping him there is no way to become him there; if one worships the guru who shows how to become him by that worship, union is possible.
2119.nuance: ஆமாறு (the way of becoming) is the hinge: worship of Siva alone gave the gods no way to become one with him; the guru shows it. The verse makes the guru the means, not a rival object of worship.

2120.reading: Seeing that men and gods, held by soul and bond, pass away through their deeds, if the one called guru is a knower without flaw, there is nothing to call him but the Supreme.
2120.nuance: The condition matters: only the flawless jnani is to be named பரம். Men and gods both fall under பசு and பாசம், so neither can be the guru by status alone.

2121.reading: The sole Lord who took them as his servants, so that love may grow and the deeds of those who took him up may go day by day, has ended them, not as one who took on the form of the tall one with water in his red locks.
2121.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are obscure. They may mean the Lord destroys his servants' deeds through the guru rather than in his own form, which would continue 2119 and 2120, but that is a guess.

links.note: Both deny that birth ranks people: the Kural says birth is alike for all and distinction comes from deeds; Tirumular says kin is one and God is one. The Kural keeps a distinction by deeds that Tirumular does not mention.
1581 says Nandi taught that the guru is Siva; 2120 adds the condition, a guru who is a flawless knower, and says such a one is to be called nothing but the Supreme.
Both make reaching the Lord the end of births: the Kural's crossing of the sea of births, Tirumular's freedom from all birth for the soul that holds the Lord in mind at death.

2102 bids one to think of the Lord even when dying (இறந்தொழி காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும்) so that the Siva way ends the soul's fluttering distress; 2108 repeats the line almost word for word (இறக்கின்ற காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும்) and names the result as Siva's state and no further birth. The near-repeat shows the thought held at death is the chapter's fixed counsel, with 2108 supplying what 2102 only implies.

2106 asks when this body came to be ours (எக்காலத்து இவ்வுடல் வந்து எமக்கு ஆனது) and bids one seek the way not to enter another body; Kural 340 asks whether the life, a lodger (துச்சில்) in the body, has no home of its own. The Kural's question about the soul's tenancy becomes in the Tirumanthiram a practice: reflecting on the body as not one's own is the way to grace and to ending further lodgings.

2107 says Hara knows 'that thing' (அப்பொருள்) that leaves one body and enters another, and that seeking the Lord even when dying (சாகின்ற போதும்) brings it to the other shore (அக்கரை); 2108 calls the same soul 'the one that flies' (பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று) and makes the result Siva's state and no further birth. Read together, the unnamed அப்பொருள் of 2107 is the flying soul of 2108, and the other shore is the end of birth.

2108 pictures the soul as 'the one that flies' (பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று), which reaches its goal if the Lord is thought of at death; Kural 338 likens the bond of body and life to a bird flying off and leaving its nest (குடம்பை தனித்து ஒழியப் புள் பறந்தற்றே). The Kural uses the flight to show how slight the bond is; the Tirumanthiram asks where the flight ends, and makes its end depend on the last thought.

2109 says that for those who stand within and know, the Lord becomes a cow long in milk after calving (நீடிய ஈற்றுப் பசு); 2627 has the devotee call the Lord as a calf calls a cow (ஆன்கன்று தேடி அழைக்கும் அதுபோல்), and the Lord comes and enters the body. Both make the Lord's giving the cow's unforced giving to its calf; 2627 adds the devotee's side, the calf's calling.

2110 says the one of unfailing fame (கேடில் புகழோன்), by whom strong deeds perish (கெடுகின்ற வல்வினை), places those who seek his feet among the celestials; Kural 5 says the two deeds born of darkness do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's true praise (பொருள்சேர் புகழ்). Both join the Lord's fame to the ending of deeds; the Tirumanthiram sets this at the moment of rising upward, which the Kural does not.

2111 repeats 1862 line for line in its first two lines (ஏறுடையாய் இறைவா எம்பிரான் என்று நீறிடுவார் அடியார் நிகழ் தேவர்கள்) and ends alike, வேறு அணிவார்க்கு வினையில்லை. The difference is the third line: in 1862 one honours the ash-wearing devotees as the Lord himself (அண்ணல் இவர் என்று), in 2111 one wears the Lord's feet (அண்ணல் திருவடி); the near-repeat moves freedom from deeds from honouring devotees to holding the feet.

2113 says there is one true austerity (மெய்த்தவம்), one true foot and one true path to take up, for those who stand wishing to take them up (வேண்டி நின்றோர்க்கே); Kural 265 says austerity is striven for here because one obtains what one wants as one wants it (வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங்கு எய்தலால்). Both tie tapas to the seeker's wanting; the Kural to what it yields, the Tirumanthiram to who may take it up.

2114 says the fire-coloured one gives joy to those who come to him (சார்ந்தவர்க்கு இன்பம்) and painful birth to those who turn away (பேர்ந்தவர்க்கு இன்னாப் பிறவி); Kural 4 says those who reach the feet of the one without liking or aversion have no suffering anywhere (அடி சேர்ந்தார்க்கு யாண்டும் இடும்பை இல). The Tirumanthiram adds the other half the Kural leaves unstated, and its verb கொடுத்திடும் puts the painful birth in the Lord's giving, where the Kural's வேண்டாமை இலான் names no aversion at all.

2115 says the Stainless one is present as ghee within milk (நெய்த்தலைப் பால்போல்) yet those who praise do not desire that light; 134 says those who grasp the guru's word beyond speech, when the body falls, mix into the shoreless light like ghee in pure milk (பாலினுள் நெய் கலந்தாற்போல்). The same image runs both ways: in 2115 the Lord is hidden in the world as ghee in milk, in 134 the freed soul is lost in the light as ghee in milk.

2118 says that if deceivers (வஞ்சகர்) stay before the true guru, famine (பஞ்சம்) comes to the land; 535 says that if falsehood enters the presence of the true guru (சற்குருச் சந்நிதி பொய்வரின்), the good path fails, knowledge does not stay and famine comes too (பஞ்சமும் ஆமே). The pair fixes the reading of 2118's doubtful text: famine as the public consequence of deceit near the guru is the book's settled claim.

1581 says Nandi taught that the guru is Siva (குருவே சிவம்); 2119 says countless gods worshipped Siva without finding the way to become him (ஆமாறு ஒன்று இல்லை), and union comes by worshipping the guru who shows that way. 2119 limits the identity of 1581 to a function: the guru counts as Siva because he shows the way of becoming, which worship of Siva alone did not give.

2120 says that since men and gods, held by soul and bond, pass away through deeds, only a flawless knower (ஞானி கோதிலன்) called guru is to be named the Supreme (பரம்); 2057 describes that guru as one of supreme bliss (பரஇன்பன்) who practises Siva-yoga and removes the soul's bonds (உயிர்பாசம் நீக்கி). 2120 gives the condition for calling a guru பரம்; 2057 spells out what such a guru does.

source_issues: 2110: சிவனார் in line 1 may be a slip for சீவனார் (the soul).
2118: சற்குறுபால் is probably for சற்குரு; the verse is doubtful throughout and may be corrupt.
2109 line 4 (ஈற்றுப் பசுவது) and 2121 lines 3 and 4 are obscure.
